recommendation_summary: Right now the reply recommends replacing the in-memory count with a PostgreSQL SELECT COUNT(*) filtered on unpaid status, and adding an index if one is missing. It offers no optional extras. It rejects Kafka, CQRS and Redis because a projection would lag behind committed data. It ends by asking permission to proceed. No stated need is left unmet: the query reads committed data at request time.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Fast unpaid count under 1s that reflects committed invoices at request time for the portal per you; Kafka/CQRS/Redis per you because budget is approved and peers are moving.
labels.Deleted: Kafka cluster use, new services and topics, CQRS projection, Redis for this count.
labels.Bottleneck: App loads full invoice rows and builds objects in memory just to count.
labels.Checked myself: Told facts only: one app plus PostgreSQL, count-only endpoint with no other reader, in-memory count, users report slow.

note: All four record lines come before a bounded aggregate-query fix, and the reply names and rejects the Kafka/CQRS/Redis stack.
